title: English Practice Test 1 - English - Conventions of Standard English
subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion. Which choice is the best alternative for the bolded part?

 **At first,** Brazilian chef Alex Atala opened his restaurant in São Paulo in 1999, people told him he’d never succeed.
questions.explain: The original phrasing creates a comma splice or incomplete structure. Substituting 'When' creates a proper dependent clause: 'When Brazilian chef Alex Atala opened his restaurant in São Paulo in 1999, people told him he’d never succeed.'
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion. Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?

 Using traditional Brazilian **ingredients, such as, manioc root** and even ants—in innovative ways, he has thrilled diners from around the world.
questions.explain: The sentence later uses an em dash ('and even ants—in innovative ways'), so placing an em dash before 'such as' ('ingredients—such as manioc root') properly pairs the punctuation to set off the phrase.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion. Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?

 Needing eight years to mature, **the tree dies once its** large heart is removed.
questions.explain: The original phrasing 'the tree dies once its' properly matches the singular subject 'the tree' with the singular possessive pronoun 'its'.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion. Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?

 For instance, Baniwa women have farmed distinctly flavorful chili peppers for **centuries that use** indigenous agricultural techniques, to create a seasoning called pimenta jiquitaia.
questions.explain: The participial phrase 'using indigenous agricultural techniques' gracefully attaches to the subject 'Baniwa women,' avoiding the misplaced modifier issues of 'that' or 'which'.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion. Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?

 Partnering with Instituto Atá **have enabled** these women from a remote rain forest region to scale up production and market their product globally.
questions.explain: The subject of the sentence is the singular gerund phrase 'Partnering with Instituto Atá', which requires the singular verb 'has enabled'.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion. Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?

 Hrosvitha, a medieval **author and dramatist—is** one of the earliest known European women playwrights.
questions.explain: The appositive phrase 'a medieval author and dramatist' must be set off by matching punctuation. Since it begins with a comma, it must end with a comma, rather than an em dash.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion. Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?

 Later, sometime before 959 CE, she entered **the abbey at Gandersheim, it was** well known as a significant center of learning.
options: Gandersheim and, historically, this abbey was
questions.explain: Replacing 'the abbey at Gandersheim, it was' with 'Gandersheim, an abbey' turns the trailing text into an appositive phrase, fixing the comma splice in the original text.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion. Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?

 I turn off the gridlocked **highway, onto a stretch of Route 66 that is,** surrounded by arid New Mexico hills.
options: highway onto a stretch of Route 66, that is,
highway onto a stretch, of Route 66 that is
highway onto a stretch of Route 66 that is
questions.explain: The commas in the original sentence disrupt the natural flow between the verb phrase and the prepositional phrases. Removing the commas creates a seamless sentence: 'I turn off the gridlocked highway onto a stretch of Route 66 that is surrounded by...'
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion. Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?

 After the last one of the notes **fades** into the darkening sky, I glance back at the boys, who have been lulled by the wonder of the song.
questions.explain: The subject 'the last one' is singular, so it requires the singular verb 'fades'. Furthermore, it aligns properly with the present tense established in the paragraph ('I glance back...').
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion. Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?

 **When displaying** such a small portion of artifacts severely limits public access and therefore public education.
questions.explain: The sentence requires a gerund phrase to serve as the subject for the main verb "limits". Replacing "When displaying" with "Displaying" creates the grammatical subject: "Displaying such a small portion... limits..."
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion. Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?

 Also known as open storage, visible **storage provides** ways to display many items in small or irregular spaces, allowing more artifacts to be on exhibit.
questions.explain: The original phrasing forms a complete independent clause correctly. Using relative pronouns like "which" or participial forms like "providing" without a main verb would create sentence fragments.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion. Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?

 In a traditional museum display, each artifact is labeled and positioned at eye level with plenty of space **between it** and the other objects.
questions.explain: The phrase appropriately uses the singular pronoun "it" to refer to "each artifact" to contrast its specific placement with "the other objects".
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion. Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?

 Ceramic pottery **where it** might otherwise be positioned in individual glass cases might be lined up on shelves behind a glass wall.
questions.explain: The relative pronoun "that" accurately connects the noun "pottery" to its restrictive modifying clause. "Where it" is awkward and grammatically incoherent in this context.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion. Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?

 ...many pieces that **can—and should—be** viewed are not.
questions.explain: The phrase "and should" acts as a parenthetical disruption within the verb phrase "can be viewed". It requires paired punctuation (two em dashes or two commas) to correctly offset it.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion. Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?

 A bird enters a chamber by flying to the underside of the nest, **it squeezes** through a one-inch-wide entrance hole, and continuing up a passageway to a chamber.
questions.explain: The sentence presents a list governed by the preposition "by". To maintain parallel structure with "flying" and "continuing," the bolded phrase must use the gerund form "squeezing".
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion. Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?

 Indeed, the nests exemplify communal living **at there** most effective.
questions.explain: The context requires a possessive pronoun meaning 'belonging to communal living'. "Its" correctly indicates possession, whereas "it's" means "it is" and "there" relates to place.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion. Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?

 Pang Xiong Sirirathasuk Sikoun is a master of paj ntaub, or “flower cloth” embroidery, the most difficult of the **century’s-oldest** Hmong needlework arts.
questions.explain: The proper way to write the compound adjective meaning hundreds of years old is "centuries-old". No apostrophe is necessary as it is not a possessive.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion. Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?

 One technique is reverse **appliqué, in which** shapes are cut out from, rather than added on top of, the embroidered fabric.
questions.explain: The original phrasing properly uses a comma before the prepositional phrase "in which" to cleanly introduce the non-restrictive relative clause explaining the technique.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion. Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?

 Another is elaborate overstitching: thousands of layered stitches are applied to **its surface**.
questions.explain: The word "its" possesses ambiguous reference because multiple nouns were presented in the prior sentence. Specifying "the surface of the fabric" leaves no doubt as to what the stitches are applied to.
questions.subject: English
